analysis:
This batch has only changelog fragments and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md. No executable source changed, so no control regression can be shown here. The changelog describes unseen code, and I did not verify those claims.

Relevant threat IDs:
- T-041/A-001: the changelog says GLM uses the encrypted SSD prefix store by default. DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 opts out. Image and video rows never reuse cached prefixes. The cache key comes from the Keychain/SE-rooted KEK. An ad hoc build reports a typed 'key_unavailable' reason. DEBUG-only DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE can supply a persistent key; the changelog says release builds omit it, which a later pass should confirm. The metrics detail string and public log line expose only the model and a reason.
- TB-007/A-004/T-012/T-027: the changelog says weight hashing now uses F_NOCACHE aligned reads with unchanged digests. It also says the coordinator catalog, revision receipt and loaded bytes must agree on one aggregate. A source pass should confirm that this is enforced.
- TB-002/T-010: new GLM capacity refusals return HTTP 503 before headers. Scratch-reservation refusals now defer instead of failing rows. The 262,144-token context bound and the 400 for oversized context are availability controls.
- TB-011/T-052: the new runtime capability glm5_next_v1 and the hardware gate (M5 Max/Ultra, 256 GB) are provider-reported. The coordinator presumably trusts them for routing. A reviewer should confirm that this self-report grants no serving authorization beyond the platform's EvaluateAuthorization.
- Local Responses continuation (previous_response_id) keeps prompt history in process memory. It is not persisted and survives no restart. hardware-support.md notes the SDK response store has no eviction (an unbounded-memory availability concern, local mode only). The threat model has no entry for this.
- GLM video/image decode is a new untrusted-media parsing surface. It is bounded by a 512 MiB decoded-frame cap and a 28,532-token cap. This resembles T-050 (temp-file plaintext exposure), so the media code needs a source-level check.

No source code was supplied for any of these. Deeper review of the Swift sources is needed.
